newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes lower on commercial sales.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes lower on commercial sales.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower on commercial selling, traders said.
"There was a good amount of commercial selling," a trader said. Wilson Trading sold 1.5 million bushels of December and LFG Futures sold one million bushels of December, traders said.
Traders also noted scattered unwinding of long KCBT/short MGE spreads and cited some trade speculation that the U.S. spring wheat crop may rebound to produce good crop yields.
"I think the spring crop is better than what the government says but they'll (crop scouts) be out there this week and I think they'll find more bushels," a trader said.
USDA's estimate for the U.S. spring crop stands at 569 million bushels, below industry expectations for 634 million.
A tour this week of the U.S. spring wheat region was expected to report uneven yield potential.
"There's a pretty big variety across the state," said Pat Berglund, director of the Northern Crops Institute, referring to the expectations for North Dakota's spring wheat production.
MGE spring wheat futures closed two to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with September down 2-1/2 at $3.82-1/2.
MGE spring wheat futures volume was estimated by the MGE at 15,494 contracts, above the 14,629 traded Friday.
Feed barley futures closed unchanged with September at $6.20 per cwt.
